queen-mate.title: Queen and king
queen-mate.text: Push the king to the edge with your queen a knight's jump away, then bring your king up. Watch out for stalemate.

two-rooks.title: Two rooks
two-rooks.text: The rooks take turns cutting off ranks — a ladder that walks the king to the edge.

rook-mate.title: Rook and king
rook-mate.text: Use the rook to box the king in and your own king to take away squares. Shrink the box move by move.

two-bishops.title: Two bishops
two-bishops.text: Side by side the bishops form a wall. Drive the king into a corner; your king must help.

bishop-knight.title: Bishop and knight
bishop-knight.text: The hardest basic mate: only the corners of the bishop's color work. Within fifty moves, please.

back-rank.title: Back rank
back-rank.text: The king is boxed in by its own pawns. One rook move ends it.

smothered.title: Smothered king
smothered.text: Surrounded by its own pieces, the king has nowhere to go. The knight finishes.

arabian.title: Rook and knight
arabian.text: A rook next to the king, protected by a knight — one of the oldest known mates.

scholars.title: Weak f7
scholars.text: Early in the game f7 is defended only by the king. Strike.

ladder.title: The ladder
ladder.text: Two rooks, two moves. One cuts off, the other mates.

legal.title: The queen as bait
legal.text: Black just won your queen. Was it worth it? Mate in two.

anastasia.title: Knight and rook
anastasia.text: The knight covers the escape squares. Open the h-file and mate.

philidor-legacy.title: The knight's dance
philidor-legacy.text: Check, double check, a queen sacrifice — and a smothered king. Mate in four.

knight-fork.title: Family fork
knight-fork.text: A knight attacks two pieces at once — especially strong when one of them is the king.

skewer.title: Skewer
skewer.text: Check the king along a line; when it steps aside, the piece behind it falls.

discovered.title: Discovered check
discovered.text: Move the knight out of the rook's way with check — and attack something at the same time.

opposition.title: Taking the opposition
opposition.text: Kings face each other with one square between them. The side that does not have to move wins the standoff.

key-squares.title: Key squares
key-squares.text: Get your king to a key square in front of the pawn and the pawn will queen by itself.

square.title: The square of the pawn
square.text: Can your king catch the pawn? Count the square from the pawn to the queening rank.

breakthrough.title: Breakthrough
breakthrough.text: Three pawns against three — sacrifice two so the third one runs through.

rook-cut.title: Rook and king (cut off)
rook-cut.text: Keep the king cut off with your rook and drive it back rank by rank.

queen-vs-pawn.title: Queen against a pawn
queen-vs-pawn.text: Check, approach, check again: force the king in front of its pawn and bring your king closer each time.

lucena.title: Building a bridge
lucena.text: The famous winning method: get your king out and use the rook to shield it from checks.

philidor.title: Third-rank defence
philidor.text: Keep your rook on the third rank from your side until the pawn advances, then check from behind.

king-in-front.title: King in front of the pawn
king-in-front.text: Stay in front of the pawn and keep the opposition. The pawn cannot pass.

wrong-bishop.title: The wrong bishop
wrong-bishop.text: The bishop does not control the queening corner. Get your king there and stay.

rook-pawn.title: Edge pawn
rook-pawn.text: With a pawn on the edge, a king in the corner is impossible to dislodge.
